newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - March 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - March 21.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Police Maj-Gen Seri Temiyavej has challenged Adnan Khashoggi to come to Thailand and defend himself against fraud charges in the Bangkok Bank of Commerce (BBC) affair. Describing the Saudi tycoon as a dangerous old man, Pol Maj-Gen Seri threw down the gauntlet after Khashoggi threatened to sue Thai authorities for accusing him of fraud. (BANGKOK POST)

- In a move against one of the largest illegal logging operations since logging was banned nationwide in 1989, forestry police have asked for permission to search a warehouse in Mae Hong Son province where it is suspected more than 600 freshly-cut teak logs are stored. The forestry police search request to the Police Department identifies the firm as Ska Bee. (THE NATION)

- Hitting back at a House committee, Deputy Finance Minister Chaturon Chaisaeng has promised to give up his Cabinet post and quit politics if his father personally gained from a planned purchase of land for the new site of Parliament. Chaturon's vow comes after Noppadol Pattama, spokesman for the House committee on parliamentary affairs, on Wednesday claimed that there were irregularities in the proposed buying of land by a House speical committee selecting the new Parliament site. (THE NATION) (BANGKOK POST)

- The Bank of Thailand (BOT) will launch an investigation into irregular transactions between finance companies and their subsidiaries that apparently benefit the management. The central bank's investigation, part of attempts to clean up the mess in financial houses, will be conducted on a broad scale that covers not only the debtors but also the listed and unlisted subsidiaries of finance companies. (THE NATION) (BANGKOK POST)

- Jalaprathan Cement, the nation's fifth largest cement producer, expects to sign a financing package with 23 local institutions within six weeks. The new financial scheme will convert Jalaprathan's call- and short-term loan facilities into medium-term loans with maturities of up to eight years. (BUSINESS DAY)
